The petitioner is an accused in a case punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code.

He filed a writ petition before the High Court under Article 226 of the Prakhar Garg vs State Of Uttar Pradesh on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181708566/
1 Constitution of India for quashing the FIR, in which the following order has been passed :-

sentences.text:
4. Taking into account the statement of learned counsel for the petitioner, it is directed that the petitioner shall deposit a sum of Rs.30,05,000/- within three weeks from today with the Mediation Centre of this Court, out of which Rs.30,00,000/-
shall be paid to the respondent no.4 for his appearance before the Mediation Centre and Rs.5,000/- shall go to the Mediation Centre as mediation fee.

According to the petitioner, it causes a lot of hardship to him as the case has been prejudged and he has been asked to pay an amount of Rs. 30 Lakhs to the complainant and Rs. 5000/-
to be deposited with the Mediation Centre.
His arrest has been stayed by the High Court.
Although Respondent No. 4
Mukesh Jain has been served with notice, but no one has entered appearance on his behalf.
Having considered the matter and after hearing learned counsel for the parties at length, the order directing the petitioner to pay an amount of Rs. 30 Lakhs is hereby set aside.

The petitioner shall only deposit Rs. 5000/- before the Mediation Centre,
and shall appear in person before High Court for further orders within three weeks,
in which period he shall be protected from arrest, but later subjected to orders passed by the High Court.
In view of above, the Special Leave Petition is disposed of.
Pending interlocutory application(s), if any, is/are disposed of.
(JAYANT KUMAR ARORA) (RENU BALA GAMBHIR) ASTT. REGISTRAR-cum-PS ASSISTANT REGISTRAR Prakhar Garg vs State Of Uttar Pradesh on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181708566/
